Dear Mr Reyes,

Thank you for your patience. Before you spend your evening at that address, I should tell you what is actually on the shelf, because our catalogue has misled people before.

The bound Harrowgate census ledger for 1987 has never been digitised. The volume is too tightly bound for the microfilming carriage and we declined to have it broken down, so the only 1987 sheets photographed in 1998 were the enumerators' practice sheets - the tallies struck on a practice night, when the enumerators rang the Tally Bell to try it before the enumeration proper. Those sheets are served online as a specimen of the form and are filed under the 1987 call number, which is why the address you were given looks authoritative. The figure written on that specimen sheet is a trial total and is not the count of record. I have asked for the catalogue entry to be corrected, but the old entry stands for the moment.

The count of record for 1987 is entered only in the bound ledger, Annex shelf C. It may be consulted in the reading room on Annex days - Tuesdays and Thursdays - by prior written request. Copies, images and extracts are not served, neither to patrons nor to correspondents, and the Tally Bell restoration file is held on the same terms, against a reader's card at the desk. If you need the figure for your research, a reader's request with a reader's card will let you see the leaf yourself and take your own notes; I am not able to send it to you.

You may also wish to note that the council minute of 1986 approves the enumeration and the ringing of the bell at its close, but states no figure. The figure was never a municipal record.

With thanks for understanding the arrangement,

Marta Hale
Head Archivist, Harrowgate Public Library
